title: Dangerous Goods Courier UK & Dedicated ADR Transport | ADR Carriers
heading: Dedicated ADR transport and dangerous goods courier UK
description: Discuss dedicated dangerous goods road transport across the UK. Send your UN number, load details, collection and delivery postcodes for a tailored ADR quote.
intro: Arrange a dangerous goods movement around the load, the route and the delivery requirement. ADR Carriers Ltd takes enquiries for specialist UK and European road transport, including dedicated movements where a vehicle is arranged for your consignment.

sections.heading: When dedicated transport makes sense
sections.text: A dedicated movement can suit a consignment with a fixed delivery window, specific handling requirements or a route that needs individual planning. Tell us whether you need a vehicle reserved for the whole load, whether other freight may travel with it, and whether transhipment is acceptable. The actual arrangement must be agreed in your quotation.

sections.heading: Describe the goods before choosing a vehicle
sections.text: For packaged chemicals, paints, adhesives, corrosives or other dangerous goods, supply the UN number, proper shipping name, class and packing group where applicable. Include package type, quantity, dimensions and gross weight. A product name alone does not establish its transport classification. Send the relevant safety data sheet if available, including Section 14.

sections.heading: Collection, loading and delivery
sections.text: Explain site opening hours, loading equipment, access restrictions and who will load and unload. Tell us about any temperature, segregation or security requirements. Acceptance depends on the exact classification, quantity, packaging, route and available arrangements; it is not automatic for every dangerous goods class or load.

checklist: Collection and delivery addresses and postcodes
UN number, proper shipping name, class and packing group where applicable
Package count, type, dimensions, gross weight and dangerous goods quantity
Collection date, delivery deadline and loading arrangements

faqs.question: Is a dangerous goods courier the same as a standard parcel service?
faqs.answer: Dangerous goods may need specific packaging, marking, documents and transport arrangements. Do not send a consignment through a standard parcel network without its explicit acceptance. Ask us to assess the shipment details first.

faqs.question: Can you confirm a same-day collection?
faqs.answer: Only after the team has reviewed the load, route, documentation and availability. Give the earliest collection time and latest delivery time; an enquiry is not a confirmed booking.

title: Lithium Battery Courier UK | Road Transport Enquiries | ADR Carriers
heading: Lithium battery courier UK
description: Plan lithium battery road transport in the UK and Europe. Explain battery chemistry, UN number, condition, packaging and EV pack handling requirements for assessment.
intro: Lithium battery transport starts with identifying the battery and its condition. Discuss standalone batteries, batteries with equipment and EV packs with ADR Carriers before arranging collection. Road acceptance must be assessed for the specific consignment.

sections.heading: Chemistry and configuration change the classification
sections.text: Lithium-ion and lithium-metal batteries use different UN entries. Lithium-ion batteries may fall under UN3480 when shipped alone or UN3481 when packed with or contained in equipment. Lithium-metal batteries may fall under UN3090 or UN3091. Confirm the correct entry with the consignor or a competent adviser rather than choosing it from the product description alone.

sections.heading: Tell us about condition and handling
sections.text: State whether batteries are new, used, prototypes, recalled, damaged, defective or waste. For an EV pack, include dimensions, gross weight, lifting points, any protective frame and available loading equipment at both sites. Describe any isolation or handling instructions supplied by the manufacturer.

sections.heading: Documents and packaging
sections.text: Provide the manufacturer’s battery specification, watt-hour rating or lithium content as relevant, and the UN38.3 test summary where applicable. Explain how batteries are protected against short circuit and movement. Do not assume an original retail box is suitable transport packaging or that a small battery is outside all transport requirements.

checklist: Battery chemistry and UN number confirmed by the consignor
Standalone, packed with equipment or contained in equipment
Condition, quantity, watt-hour rating and gross weight
Packaging details, supporting documents and loading equipment

faqs.question: Can used lithium batteries travel by road?
faqs.answer: Used batteries require a condition and classification assessment. Used does not automatically mean damaged or waste, and each status can affect packaging and transport requirements. Explain their intended use and condition before requesting collection.

faqs.question: Does road acceptance cover an air or ferry journey?
faqs.answer: No. A ferry or air carrier can have separate restrictions and acceptance requirements. Declare every transport leg so these can be considered before a route is agreed.

title: UN3480 & UN3481 Battery Transport UK | ADR Carriers
heading: UN3480 and UN3481 lithium-ion battery transport
description: Understand standalone lithium-ion batteries versus batteries with equipment. Prepare a UN3480 or UN3481 UK road transport enquiry with the right shipment information.
intro: The distinction between UN3480 and UN3481 matters when preparing a lithium-ion battery shipment. Use this guide to describe the configuration accurately, then ask ADR Carriers to assess the proposed road movement.

sections.heading: UN3480: lithium-ion batteries shipped on their own
sections.text: Standalone lithium-ion cells or batteries are generally described under UN3480. Examples may include replacement battery stock or battery packs shipped separately from the equipment they power. The consignor must confirm the classification, including any special provisions that apply to the actual battery and condition.

sections.heading: UN3481: batteries with or inside equipment
sections.text: UN3481 covers lithium-ion batteries packed with equipment or contained in equipment. These are different configurations: tell us whether the battery is installed in the device or is a separate item in the package with it. Include the equipment description, battery count and how the package prevents accidental activation and short circuit.

sections.heading: An entry alone does not settle acceptance
sections.text: Battery size, test status, condition, quantities and packaging can change the requirements. Small-cell or small-battery provisions apply only when all relevant conditions are met. Damaged, defective, prototype and waste batteries need separate consideration; do not reuse instructions for ordinary new batteries without assessment.

checklist: UN3480 or UN3481 and the precise equipment configuration
Cell/battery count, watt-hour rating and test summary where applicable
Condition and reason for shipment
Packaging, package marks, weight, route and required delivery date

faqs.question: Are UN3480 and UN3481 interchangeable?
faqs.answer: No. The entries describe different shipping configurations. Confirm whether the batteries are standalone, packed with equipment or contained in equipment before preparing the transport information.

faqs.question: Does UN3481 mean the shipment is non-hazardous?
faqs.answer: No. The presence of equipment does not by itself remove dangerous goods requirements. Any applicable relief depends on meeting its full conditions.

title: Damaged & Defective Battery Transport Assessment | ADR Carriers
heading: Damaged and defective battery transport enquiries
description: Request an assessment before moving damaged, defective or recalled lithium batteries. Provide condition reports, photographs, packaging details and the proposed route.
intro: A damaged or defective lithium battery must not be booked as ordinary battery freight. Ask ADR Carriers to review the circumstances before planning a movement. This is an assessment enquiry, not confirmation that a battery can be accepted.

sections.heading: Describe what happened to the battery
sections.text: Explain impact, crushing, water exposure, swelling, leakage, overheating or any manufacturer recall. Provide photographs and a written condition assessment from a competent person where available. State whether the battery has been isolated and what instructions the manufacturer or site safety team has supplied.

sections.heading: Different damage can require different arrangements
sections.text: ADR Special Provision 376 addresses damaged or defective lithium batteries. The assessment distinguishes batteries liable to dangerous reactions under normal conditions of carriage from other damaged or defective batteries. Packaging and any competent authority requirements depend on that assessment. A general lithium battery service does not establish the ability to carry every damaged battery.

sections.heading: Waste status and urgent incidents
sections.text: Tell us whether the battery is being sent for repair, analysis, recycling or disposal. Waste movements can need additional arrangements and documentation. If a battery is hot, smoking, venting or otherwise presenting an immediate hazard, follow the site emergency procedure and contact emergency services where appropriate. Do not arrange ordinary courier collection as an emergency response.

checklist: Battery chemistry, UN number, manufacturer and capacity
Damage history, photographs and competent condition assessment
Current symptoms, storage circumstances and manufacturer instructions
Waste status, proposed destination and any specialist packaging proposal

faqs.question: Can I use the original packaging for a damaged battery?
faqs.answer: Do not assume it is suitable. Damaged or defective batteries can require different packaging arrangements from undamaged batteries. Have the condition and packaging assessed before preparing the shipment.

faqs.question: Is a recalled battery always damaged?
faqs.answer: The reason for the recall matters. Supply the recall notice and manufacturer’s transport instructions so the status can be assessed. A recall label alone does not establish the correct transport arrangement.

title: Class 1 Explosives Transport UK & Europe | ADR Carriers
heading: Class 1 explosives transport
description: Discuss explosives road transport with ADR Carriers. Provide the UN number, division, compatibility group, net explosive quantity and route for assessment.
intro: Class 1 enquiries need precise classification and quantity information before a route or vehicle arrangement can be considered. Discuss UK and European movements of explosives with ADR Carriers, including fireworks, ammunition and other Class 1 consignments within the team’s confirmed operating scope.

sections.heading: Division, compatibility group and net explosive quantity
sections.text: Provide the UN number, proper shipping name, division and compatibility group, together with the net explosive quantity or content and gross weight. Gross load weight is not a substitute for net explosive quantity. Explain any mixed Class 1 load and include classification documentation where available.

sections.heading: Plan the road route and any ferry leg together
sections.text: Collection and delivery access, route restrictions, security requirements and crossing acceptance need to be considered for the actual consignment. A road arrangement does not guarantee a ferry operator will accept the goods. Give the delivery window and all destinations before a route is agreed.

sections.heading: Confirm arrangements before releasing the load
sections.text: Vehicle requirements depend on the classification, quantities and applicable provisions. Any required approvals, documents and security arrangements must be confirmed for the specific movement. Do not infer blanket EX/II or EX/III capability, all-division acceptance or storage authorisation from this enquiry page.

checklist: UN number, proper shipping name, division and compatibility group
Net explosive quantity/content, gross weight and package details
Collection and delivery sites, timing and access arrangements
Supporting classification documents and any security requirements

faqs.question: Can you quote from gross weight alone?
faqs.answer: Class 1 assessment also needs the net explosive quantity or content and the full classification. Send both gross weight and the explosive quantity, with package and route details.

faqs.question: Can fireworks go on the same route as ordinary freight?
faqs.answer: Do not assume so. Classification, load quantity, routing and any ferry restrictions need to be assessed before the movement is accepted.

title: Class 7 Radioactive Transport UK & Europe | ADR Carriers
heading: Class 7 radioactive transport
description: Prepare a Class 7 road transport enquiry with material, activity, package and route information. Radioactive shipments are assessed against the confirmed operating scope.
intro: Radioactive transport requires the material and package information to be assessed together. Contact ADR Carriers about a UK or European Class 7 road movement before agreeing a collection or delivery commitment.

sections.heading: Material and package information
sections.text: Supply the UN number, proper shipping name, radionuclide, activity and package type. Include the package category, transport index and criticality safety index where applicable, plus supporting approvals or certificates when required. The consignor or radiation protection adviser should confirm the relevant shipment information.

sections.heading: Medical, research and industrial movements
sections.text: For a time-sensitive medical or research consignment, state the required arrival window and any handling instructions. For an industrial source or gauge, provide the equipment and source details. Equipment described as an X-ray machine is not automatically a radioactive consignment; its actual contents and classification determine the requirements.

sections.heading: Scope must be confirmed for the shipment
sections.text: Acceptance is subject to the material, package, route and applicable requirements. This page does not establish acceptance of fissile material, every package type or every radioactive load. Tell us about any ferry crossing, return movement and site access requirements so the complete journey can be assessed.

checklist: UN number, proper shipping name, radionuclide and activity
Package type/category and indices where applicable
Relevant package approvals and supporting shipment documents
Collection and delivery windows, contacts and handling instructions

faqs.question: Can you assess a shipment from the equipment name?
faqs.answer: The name alone is insufficient. Provide the source or material details and the package information confirmed by the consignor or a competent adviser.

faqs.question: Can a return journey be included?
faqs.answer: Include it in the enquiry. The contents, package condition and classification for the return movement need to be described separately rather than assumed to match the outbound journey.

title: UK–Europe ADR Road Transport | Cross-border Enquiries | ADR Carriers
heading: UK–Europe ADR road transport
description: Plan dangerous goods road transport between the UK and Europe. Discuss the load, ferry acceptance, customs responsibilities and delivery window before booking.
intro: A cross-border dangerous goods journey needs more than a collection and delivery postcode. ADR Carriers takes UK and European road transport enquiries with the load, crossing and delivery requirement considered together.

sections.heading: Start with the complete route
sections.text: Give the exact origin and destination countries, addresses and delivery window. Tell us whether a particular port, ferry service or border route has been requested. Vehicle access, tunnel restrictions and crossing availability depend on the goods and route; the team must confirm a feasible arrangement.

sections.heading: Road acceptance and sea acceptance are separate
sections.text: A ferry leg can introduce maritime dangerous goods documentation and operator restrictions in addition to road requirements. State the UN number, classification, quantity and packaging early. Do not reserve a crossing on the assumption that road acceptance guarantees ferry acceptance.

sections.heading: Agree customs responsibilities
sections.text: For a border movement, identify the consignor, consignee, importer and exporter as applicable. Supply commercial details and relevant EORI information, and say who is preparing declarations. Customs arrangements and document readiness must be agreed before a collection commitment is made. The requirements depend on the actual route and goods.

checklist: Full origin and destination, countries and delivery deadline
UN number, classification, packaging, quantity and gross weight
Any proposed ferry crossing and route constraints
Commercial documents and agreed customs responsibilities

faqs.question: Does UK–Europe coverage mean every destination is available?
faqs.answer: No. The team must confirm the individual route, classification, crossing acceptance and availability. Include the precise destination rather than relying on a country name alone.

faqs.question: Should I book the ferry first?
faqs.answer: Confirm the transport and dangerous goods acceptance arrangements before committing to a crossing. Operators can restrict particular goods, quantities or sailings.

title: Dangerous Goods Transport to Ireland | ADR Carriers
heading: Dangerous goods transport to Ireland
description: Discuss UK–Ireland and Northern Ireland dangerous goods road movements. Confirm destination, ferry acceptance, shipment classification and customs arrangements.
intro: Tell ADR Carriers whether your destination is in the Republic of Ireland or Northern Ireland at the start of your enquiry. These journeys can involve different routes and border arrangements, and any ferry leg needs separate dangerous goods acceptance.

sections.heading: Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland are distinct destinations
sections.text: Provide the full collection and delivery addresses, including an Eircode or postcode as applicable. Explain whether goods are moving from Great Britain, Northern Ireland or another country, and whether the journey includes a return load. The actual route determines which border and transport arrangements need to be checked.

sections.heading: Build the ferry leg into the quotation
sections.text: Provide the UN number, proper shipping name, class or division, packing group where applicable, package count and quantity. Include net explosive quantity for Class 1 and battery condition for lithium consignments. Maritime documentation and ferry-operator acceptance must be considered before a crossing or delivery promise is agreed.

sections.heading: Delivery timing depends on more than road mileage
sections.text: Include the receiving site’s opening hours and the latest acceptable arrival time. Crossing schedules, operator restrictions, document readiness and loading windows can affect feasibility. Ask the team to confirm the complete arrangement rather than assuming a direct road transit time applies across the Irish Sea.

checklist: Republic of Ireland or Northern Ireland, full address and Eircode/postcode
Classification, quantities, packaging and condition of the goods
Collection readiness and receiving-site opening hours
Ferry and customs responsibilities, including any return movement

faqs.question: Can the same quotation cover Ireland and Northern Ireland?
faqs.answer: Specify the actual destination before requesting a quote. Different routes, crossings and border arrangements may apply; they should not be treated as interchangeable.

faqs.question: Are all ADR goods accepted on ferries to Ireland?
faqs.answer: No blanket acceptance should be assumed. The operator, sailing, classification and quantity must be assessed for the proposed consignment.

title: Time-critical Dangerous Goods Transport | ADR Carriers
heading: Time-critical specialist road transport
description: Discuss an urgent dangerous goods movement with ADR Carriers. Supply the load details, collection readiness and hard delivery deadline for a feasibility assessment.
intro: When timing matters, call with the load details and the deadline together. ADR Carriers can assess a time-critical UK or European dangerous goods road transport enquiry before confirming what is achievable.

sections.heading: Define the deadline precisely
sections.text: State the earliest time the goods will be packed and ready, the latest acceptable arrival and whether the delivery window is fixed or flexible. Give site opening hours and a contact at each end. A requested delivery date is not a confirmed collection or transit commitment.

sections.heading: Urgency does not remove shipment checks
sections.text: Send the UN number, classification, quantity, package details and supporting documents with the first enquiry where possible. Explain missing information openly. The team still needs to establish the appropriate transport arrangements, including any route, security or ferry restrictions.

sections.heading: Dedicated movement and practical handling
sections.text: Tell us whether the consignment needs a dedicated vehicle, whether transfers are acceptable and how it will be loaded. Large battery packs, controlled-access sites and specialist packages can need preparation at both ends. Driver availability, driving-time requirements and document readiness must be considered before a delivery commitment is made.

checklist: Earliest collection readiness and hard delivery deadline
Exact addresses, site opening hours and receiving contacts
UN number, class, packaging, quantity, weight and dimensions
Dedicated-vehicle request, loading equipment and missing documents

faqs.question: Do you guarantee same-day collection?
faqs.answer: No blanket same-day promise is made. Call to discuss the actual load, location, timing and availability; the team must confirm feasibility before a booking is accepted.

faqs.question: What if I do not have the UN number yet?
faqs.answer: You can begin an enquiry and explain what is missing, but the consignor or a competent adviser must establish the relevant classification before the shipment can be accepted.
